Let $X$ be a ringed space.
Let $U \subset X$ be an open subspace.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\mathcal{I}$ is an injective $\mathcal{O}_X$-module
then $\mathcal{I}|_U$ is an injective $\mathcal{O}_U$-module.
\item For any sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules $\mathcal{F}$ we have
$H^p(U, \mathcal{F}) = H^p(U, \mathcal{F}|_U)$.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: $X$ is a ringed space; $U\subseteq X$ is open.
conclusions: Injective $\mathcal O_X$-modules restrict to injective $\mathcal O_U$-modules.
For any $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ and degree $p$, $H^p(U,\mathcal F)$ computed on $X$ agrees with $H^p(U,\mathcal F|_U)$ computed on $U$.
semantic_review_note: For any ringed X and open U, restrictions of injective O_X-modules remain injective over O_U. The second source assertion identifies cohomology of a sheaf on U computed by restricting from X with intrinsic O_U-cohomology. Both independent clauses survive in the final statement.

\label{lemma-kill-cohomology-class-on-covering}
Let $X$ be a ringed space.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
Let $U \subset X$ be an open subspace.
Let $n > 0$ and let $\xi \in H^n(U, \mathcal{F})$.
Then there exists an open covering
$U = \bigcup_{i\in I} U_i$ such that $\xi|_{U_i} = 0$ for
all $i \in I$.
statement:
Let $X$ be a ringed space.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
Let $U \subset X$ be an open subspace.
Let $n > 0$ and let $\xi \in H^n(U, \mathcal{F})$.
Then there exists an open covering
$U = \bigcup_{i\in I} U_i$ such that $\xi|_{U_i} = 0$ for
all $i \in I$.
hypotheses: $X$ is a ringed space, $\mathcal F$ is an $\mathcal O_X$-module, $U\subseteq X$ is open, $n>0$, and $\xi\in H^n(U,\mathcal F)$.
conclusions: There is an open cover $U=\bigcup_i U_i$ on which each restriction $\xi|_{U_i}$ vanishes.
semantic_review_note: A positive-degree sheaf-cohomology class ξ∈H^n(U,F) of an open U in a ringed space vanishes after restricting to some open covering of U. The final assertion keeps n>0 and the existential cover with vanishing on every member; it does not claim global vanishing.
